119th CONGRESS
  2d Session
                               H. R. 10781

  To amend title 36, United States Code, to request the President to 
 designate a month each year as National American History and Founders 
                                 Month.


_______________________________________________________________________


                    IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES

                            October 9, 2026

    Mr. Haridopolos (for himself and Ms. McClellan) introduced the 
  following bill; which was referred to the Committee on the Judiciary

_______________________________________________________________________

                                 A BILL


 
  To amend title 36, United States Code, to request the President to 
 designate a month each year as National American History and Founders 
                                 Month.

    Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the 
United States of America in Congress assembled,

SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE.

    This Act may be cited as the ``National American History and 
Founders Month Act''.

SEC. 2. FINDINGS.

    Congress finds the following:
            (1) As the United States celebrates the 250th anniversary 
        of the signing of the Declaration of Independence in 2026, the 
        United States is a Nation characterized by cultural and 
        geographic diversity and uniquely bound by a common heritage 
        and history that began on July 4, 1776, with the profound words 
        of the Declaration of Independence.
            (2) The preservation and understanding of the history of 
        the United States and the principles of the Founding Fathers 
        are intrinsic values that unite the people of the United States 
        and provide a foundation for understanding the origins and 
        ideals of the United States by providing a common bond.
            (3) Presidents George Washington and Thomas Jefferson 
        stressed the crucial role of an informed citizenry in a free 
        society. They believed that an educated and knowledgeable 
        citizenry was essential for the survival of a democratic 
        republic and for the preservation of liberty.
            (4) Civics education in the United States has experienced a 
        significant decline, with only 13 percent of eighth graders 
        proficient in United States history and 22 percent of eighth 
        graders proficient in civics, according to the 2022 National 
        Assessment of Educational Progress.
            (5) A decline in civics education impairs the ability of 
        young people of the United States to engage meaningfully with 
        public officials and appreciate the philosophical foundations 
        of the American Revolutionary period, the Declaration of 
        Independence, the Constitution of the United States, and the 
        Bill of Rights.
            (6) Civics education for students can raise awareness of 
        the significant events, influential figures, and philosophical 
        bases that shaped the United States, inspiring a renewed 
        appreciation for its rich history.
            (7) Educational and service organizations in law, political 
        science, and related fields should be encouraged to support the 
        study of the history of the United States to cultivate informed 
        and engaged citizens to understand the documents that define 
        the United States, including the Declaration of Independence, 
        the Constitution of the United States, and the Bill of Rights.
            (8) Designating a month as National American History and 
        Founders Month would also aid in the discovery, collection, and 
        preservation of historical records, documents, monuments, and 
        structures that illuminate the history of the first founders 
        and their descendants.
            (9) November is the month during which the United States 
        celebrates Thanksgiving. President George Washington issued the 
        first national Thanksgiving proclamation designating Thursday, 
        November 26, 1789, as a day of public prayer and gratitude for 
        the United States. Abraham Lincoln issued a proclamation 
        officially establishing Thanksgiving Day as a national holiday 
        to designate the last Thursday of November as a day for 
        thanksgiving and unity. Designating a month as National 
        American History and Founders Month would extend this tradition 
        of unity and gratitude for the United States by deepening the 
        understanding and appreciation for the United States by the 
        people of the United States.
            (10) A permanent designation of a National American History 
        and Founders Month would encourage schools, communities, and 
        organizations to host events, educational programs, and 
        initiatives that celebrate and teach the history of the United 
        States and the contributions of the Founding Fathers.
            (11) The unique circumstances and events that created the 
        United States must be well known by the citizenry of the United 
        States so as to perpetuate into the future the values and 
        rights of the United States of individual freedom, liberty, and 
        the pursuit of happiness.
            (12) Such a designation will inspire young people of the 
        United States to learn about and take pride in the history of 
        the United States, fostering a sense of unity and shared 
        purpose.

SEC. 3. DESIGNATION.

    (a) In General.--Chapter 1 of part A of subtitle I of title 36, 
United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:
``Sec. 149. National American History and Founders Month
    ``The President is requested each year to designate a month as 
National American History and Founders Month and to call on the people 
of the United States, and the chief executive officers of each State of 
the United States, the District of Columbia, and each territory and 
possession of the United States are requested to issue each year 
proclamations calling on the people of their respective jurisdictions, 
to observe such Month with appropriate programs, ceremonies, and 
activities that enhance civics education and historical literacy.''.
    (b) Clerical Amendment.--The table of sections for chapter 1 of 
part A of subtitle I of title 36, United States Code, is amended by 
adding at the end the following:

``149. National American History and Founders Month.''.

119th CONGRESS
  2d Session
                               H. R. 10791

  To prohibit Federal funds from being provided to any State or local 
 government that celebrates Indigenous Peoples Day instead of Columbus 
                      Day, and for other purposes.


_______________________________________________________________________


                    IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES

                            October 9, 2026

  Mr. Rulli introduced the following bill; which was referred to the 
              Committee on Oversight and Government Reform

_______________________________________________________________________

                                 A BILL


 
  To prohibit Federal funds from being provided to any State or local 
 government that celebrates Indigenous Peoples Day instead of Columbus 
                      Day, and for other purposes.

    Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the 
United States of America in Congress assembled,

SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE.

    This Act may be cited as the ``Italian Heroes and Heritage Act''.

SEC. 2. FINDINGS; SENSE OF CONGRESS.

    (a) Findings.--The Congress finds the following:
            (1) Christopher Columbus set sail 534 years ago in 1492 to 
        bravely cross the Atlantic Ocean and discovered new land that 
        would soon after become known as America.
            (2) President Benjamin Harrison founded Christopher 
        Columbus day in 1892 to honor Christopher Columbus's voyage and 
        the 11 Italian-Americans murdered by a New Orleans lynch mob 
        due to suspicion and hatred of Italian-Americans.
            (3) The 11 people brutally murdered were Italian-American 
        cobbler Pietro Monasterio; fruit importer Joseph P. Macheca; 
        fruit peddlers Antonio Bagnetto, Antonio Marchesi, Antonio 
        Scaffidi; rice plantation laborer Charles Traina; stevedores 
        James Caruso and Rocco Geraci; street vendor Emmanuele Polizzi; 
        tinsmith Loreto Comitis; and ward politician Frank Romero.
    (b) Sense of Congress.--It is the sense of Congress that October 
12th should continue to be celebrated nationwide as Christopher 
Columbus Day, as it has been since 1892, to honor our Italian-American 
heritage and our forefather, Christopher Columbus, who helped to 
discover this great land.

SEC. 3. PROHIBITION ON PROVIDING FEDERAL FUNDS TO LOCAL GOVERNMENTS 
              THAT CELEBRATE INDIGENOUS PEOPLES DAY INSTEAD OF COLUMBUS 
              DAY.

    Notwithstanding any other provision of law, during the 1-year 
period beginning after October 12, 2026, and each Columbus Day (as 
described in section 6103(a) of title 5, United States Code) 
thereafter, no Federal funds may be obligated, expended, or otherwise 
dispursed to any State or unit of local government that celebrates 
Indigenous Peoples Day in lieu of Columbus Day.

119th CONGRESS

                               H. R. 10792

    To provide incentives for and protect whistleblowers under the 
   authority of the Federal Trade Commission, and for other purposes.


_______________________________________________________________________


                    IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES

                            October 9, 2026

Ms. Schakowsky (for herself, Mrs. Trahan, and Mr. Kean) introduced the 
 following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Education and 
Workforce, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for 
a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for 
consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the 
                          committee concerned

_______________________________________________________________________

                                 A BILL


 
    To provide incentives for and protect whistleblowers under the 
   authority of the Federal Trade Commission, and for other purposes.

    Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the 
United States of America in Congress assembled,

SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE.

    This Act may be cited as the ``FTC Whistleblower Act of 2026''.

SEC. 2. PROTECTION OF WHISTLEBLOWERS.

    (a) Protection From Retaliation.--A covered entity may not, 
directly or indirectly, discharge, demote, suspend, threaten, harass, 
or in any other manner discriminate or take an adverse personnel action 
against an individual (or a group of individuals) because the 
individual (or group of individuals) does any of the following:
            (1) Makes (or the covered entity suspects the individual or 
        group of individuals has made or will make) a covered 
        disclosure to--
                    (A) a qualified entity;
                    (B) a person with supervisory authority over the 
                individual (or group of individuals); or
                    (C) another individual working for the covered 
                entity who the individual (or group of individuals) 
                reasonably believes has the authority to investigate, 
                discover, or terminate the alleged violation in the 
                covered disclosure or to take any other action to 
                address such violation.
            (2) Initiates, testifies, assists, or participates (or the 
        covered entity expects will initiate, testify, assist, or 
        participate) in an investigation conducted by a qualified 
        entity or a judicial or administrative proceeding brought by a 
        qualified entity relating to a covered violation.
            (3) Objects to, or refuses to participate in, any activity, 
        policy, practice, or assigned task that the individual (or 
        group of individuals) reasonably believes is an alleged covered 
        violation.
    (b) Enforcement.--
            (1) Cause of action.--A whistleblower who alleges discharge 
        or other discrimination by a covered entity in violation of 
        subsection (a)--
                    (A) may bring an action governed by the procedures 
                and burdens of proof in section 4712 of title 41, 
                United States Code; or
                    (B) may bring an action in the appropriate district 
                court of the United States--
                            (i) for the relief described in subsection 
                        (c);
                            (ii) governed by the burdens of proof in 
                        section 1221(e) of title 5, United States Code; 
                        and
                            (iii) in which the whistleblower shall be 
                        entitled to a trial by jury.
            (2) Statute of limitations.--
                    (A) In general.--An action under paragraph (1) may 
                not be brought--
                            (i) more than 6 years after the date on 
                        which the violation of subsection (a) occurred; 
                        or
                            (ii) more than 3 years after the date on 
                        which facts material to the right of action are 
                        known or reasonably should have been known by 
                        the whistleblower alleging a violation of 
                        subsection (a).
                    (B) Required action within 10 years.--
                Notwithstanding subparagraph (A), an action under 
                paragraph (1) may not be brought more than 10 years 
                after the date on which the violation of subsection (a) 
                occurred.
            (3) Waiver of rights and remedies.--The rights and remedies 
        provided in this section may not be waived by any policy, 
        written document, or other condition relating to employment, 
        including by a predispute arbitration agreement.
            (4) Predispute arbitration agreements.--Notwithstanding any 
        other provision of law, a predispute arbitration agreement may 
        not be enforced with respect to an action under paragraph (1).
            (5) Restrictive covenant agreements.--Notwithstanding any 
        other provision of law, an agreement in which a whistleblower 
        is restrained by the covered entity that was the subject of a 
        covered disclosure from exercising a lawful profession, trade, 
        or business of any kind may not be enforced.
    (c) Relief.--Relief for any whistleblower who prevails in an action 
brought under subsection (b)(1) shall include--
            (1) reinstatement with the same seniority status that the 
        whistleblower would have had but for the discharge or 
        discrimination;
            (2) 3 times the amount of back pay owed to the 
        whistleblower, with interest; and
            (3) consequential and compensatory damages and compensation 
        for litigation costs, expert witness fees, and reasonable 
        attorneys' fees.
    (d) Communications.--
            (1) Prohibition on impeding covered disclosure.--A covered 
        entity may not take any action that impedes or prevents an 
        individual from communicating directly with a qualified entity 
        about a covered disclosure, including enforcing, or threatening 
        to enforce, a confidentiality or non-disparagement agreement.
            (2) Communication with qualified entities.--A covered 
        entity may not require the consent of the counsel of the 
        covered entity for a qualified entity to communicate directly 
        with an individual or the attorney of an individual (if the 
        individual is represented by an attorney) regarding a possible 
        covered disclosure.
            (3) Enforcement by commission.--
                    (A) Unfair or deceptive acts or practices.--A 
                violation of paragraph (1) or (2) shall be treated as a 
                violation of a regulation under section 18(a)(1)(B) of 
                the Federal Trade Commission Act (15 U.S.C. 
                57a(a)(1)(B)) regarding unfair or deceptive acts or 
                practices.
                    (B) Powers of commission.--The Commission shall 
                enforce paragraphs (1) and (2) in the same manner, by 
                the same means, and with the same jurisdiction, powers, 
                and duties as though all applicable terms and 
                provisions of the Federal Trade Commission Act (15 
                U.S.C. 41 et seq.) were incorporated into and made a 
                part of this subsection, and any person who violates 
                paragraph (1) or (2) shall be subject to the penalties 
                and entitled to the privileges and immunities provided 
                in the Federal Trade Commission Act.
    (e) Confidentiality.--
            (1) Requirement.--The Commission, any employee of the 
        Commission, and any other entity to which the Commission 
        communicates may not disclose any information provided to the 
        Commission, including information provided by a whistleblower, 
        that could reasonably be expected to reveal the identity of a 
        whistleblower.
            (2) Exception.--Notwithstanding paragraph (1), if release 
        of the information described in paragraph (1) is required by 
        law, the whistleblower shall receive timely advance notice 
        before such release.
            (3) Rules of construction.--This paragraph may not be 
        construed to prohibit--
                    (A) any disclosure described in section 21(d) of 
                the Federal Trade Commission Act (15 U.S.C. 57b-2(d));
                    (B) a disclosure to any officer or employee of a 
                Federal or State law enforcement agency or a foreign 
                law enforcement agency under section 6(f) or 21(b)(6) 
                of the Federal Trade Commission Act (15 U.S.C. 46(f), 
                57b-2(b)(6)); or
                    (C) a disclosure to which the whistleblower 
                consents.
    (f) Rules of Construction.--
            (1) Collective bargaining.--Nothing in this section may be 
        construed to diminish the rights, privileges, or remedies of 
        any whistleblower under any Federal or State law relating to 
        collective bargaining or under any collective bargaining 
        agreement.
            (2) Other whistleblower protections.--
                    (A) Nothing in this section may be construed to 
                preempt or supersede any other Federal or State law 
                relating to whistleblower protections.
                    (B) Notwithstanding any other provision of law, a 
                whistleblower shall be immune from civil and criminal 
                liability for making a covered disclosure if the 
                whistleblower would be protected from reprisal under 
                section (a). The whistleblower shall bear the burden 
                required under subsection (b) of proving that the 
                whistleblower would be protected from reprisal under 
                subsection (a) for making the disclosure. This section 
                does not provide a defense against activities unrelated 
                to conduct protected under subsection (a).
            (3) Authority of commission.--Nothing in this section may 
        be construed to limit the authority of the Commission under any 
        other provision of law.

SEC. 3. INCENTIVES FOR WHISTLEBLOWERS.

    (a) Awards.--
            (1) In general.--If a whistleblower (or group of 
        whistleblowers) voluntarily provides to the Commission original 
        information regarding an alleged covered violation and such 
        original information leads to the successful resolution of a 
        covered action, the Commission, subject to subsection (b), 
        shall pay an award to the whistleblower (or group of 
        whistleblowers) in an aggregate amount of--
                    (A) not less than 10 percent, in total, of 
                collected monetary sanctions imposed as a result of the 
                relevant covered action; and
                    (B) not more than 30 percent, in total, of 
                collected monetary sanctions imposed as a result of the 
                relevant covered action.
            (2) Payment of awards.--Any amount paid under paragraph (1) 
        shall be paid from the Fund.
    (b) Determination and Denial of Awards.--
            (1) Determination of awards.--
                    (A) Discretion.--The determination of the amount of 
                an award to be made pursuant to subsection (a) shall be 
                within the discretion of the Commission (subject to the 
                requirements described in subsection (a)).
                    (B) Criteria.--In determining an award to be made 
                pursuant to subsection (a), the Commission--
                            (i) shall take into consideration--
                                    (I) the significance of the 
                                original information provided by the 
                                whistleblower to the successful 
                                resolution of the covered action;
                                    (II) the degree of assistance 
                                provided by the whistleblower and any 
                                legal representative of the 
                                whistleblower in the covered action; 
                                and
                                    (III) such additional factors as 
                                the Commission may establish; and
                            (ii) shall not take into consideration the 
                        balance of the Fund.
            (2) Denial of awards.--Notwithstanding subsection (a), the 
        Commission shall deny an award to any whistleblower to whom an 
        award otherwise would be made pursuant to subsection (a) if the 
        whistleblower--
                    (A) is convicted of a criminal violation related to 
                the relevant covered action;
                    (B) acts without direction from a covered entity 
                (or an agent of a covered entity) to deliberately cause 
                or substantially contribute to the alleged covered 
                violation underlying the relevant covered action;
                    (C) fails to provide the relevant original 
                information to the Commission in the form the 
                Commission requires; and
                    (D) was, at the time the whistleblower acquired the 
                relevant original information, a member, officer, or 
                employee of the Commission or a law enforcement agency 
                and acquired the information while acting in the normal 
                course of the employment duties of the whistleblower.
    (c) Representation.--
            (1) Permitted representation.--A whistleblower may be 
        represented by counsel.
            (2) Required representation.--
                    (A) Anonymous claims.--Any whistleblower who 
                anonymously makes a claim for an award under subsection 
                (a) shall be represented by counsel if the 
                whistleblower anonymously submits the original 
                information upon which the claim is based.
                    (B) Disclosure of identity.--Before the payment of 
                an award described in subparagraph (A), the 
                whistleblower shall disclose the identity of the 
                whistleblower and provide such other information as the 
                Commission may require, directly or through counsel for 
                the whistleblower.
    (d) No Contract Necessary.--A contract with the Commission is not 
necessary for a whistleblower to receive an award pursuant to 
subsection (a).
    (e) Provision of False Information.--A whistleblower who knowingly 
and intentionally makes any false, fictitious, or fraudulent statement 
or representation, or who knowingly and intentionally makes or uses any 
false writing or document containing any false, fictitious, or 
fraudulent statement or entry, may not receive an award pursuant to 
subsection (a).
    (f) Appeals.--
            (1) In general.--Any determination made under this section, 
        including whether, to whom, or in what amount to make an award, 
        shall be in the discretion of the Commission.
            (2) Appeals.--Any determination made by the Commission 
        under this section may be appealed by a whistleblower to the 
        appropriate court of appeals of the United States not later 
        than 30 days after the date on which the determination is 
        issued by the Commission.
            (3) Review.--The court shall review the determination made 
        by the Commission in accordance with section 706 of title 5, 
        United States Code.
    (g) Federal Trade Commission Consumer Protection Fund.--
            (1) Establishment.--There is established in the Treasury of 
        the United States a Fund to be known as the ``Federal Trade 
        Commission Consumer Protection Fund''.
            (2) Use of fund.--The Fund shall be available to the 
        Commission, without further appropriation or fiscal year 
        limitation, in order to pay for awards made to whistleblowers 
        pursuant to subsection (a).
            (3) Deposits and credits.--
                    (A) In general.--There shall be deposited into or 
                credited to the Fund an amount equal to any monetary 
                sanctions collected by the Commission in any covered 
                action, unless the balance of the Fund at the time the 
                monetary sanction is collected exceeds $500,000,000.
                    (B) Additional amounts.--If the amounts deposited 
                into or credited to the Fund under subparagraph (A) are 
                not sufficient to pay an award made pursuant to 
                subsection (a), there shall be deposited into or 
                credited to the Fund an amount equal to the unsatisfied 
                portion of the award from any monetary sanctions 
                collected by the Commission in the covered action on 
                which the award is based.
            (4) Investments.--
                    (A) Amounts in fund.--The Commission may request 
                the Secretary of the Treasury to invest the portion of 
                the Fund that is not required to meet the current needs 
                of the Fund (as determined by the Commission).
                    (B) Eligible investments.--Investments shall be 
                made by the Secretary of the Treasury in obligations of 
                the United States or obligations that are guaranteed as 
                to principal and interest by the United States, with 
                maturities suitable to the needs of the Fund (as 
                determined by the Commission).
                    (C) Interest and proceeds credited.--The interest 
                on, and the proceeds from, the sale or redemption of 
                any obligations held in the Fund shall be credited to, 
                and form a part of, the Fund.
            (5) Reports to congress.--Not later than October 30 of each 
        year, the Commission shall submit to the Committee on Energy 
        and Commerce of the House of Representatives and the Committee 
        on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate a report 
        on--
                    (A) the whistleblower award program established 
                under this section, including a description of the 
                number of awards made pursuant to subsection (a) and 
                the types of cases in which such awards were made 
                during the preceding fiscal year;
                    (B) the balance of the Fund at the beginning of the 
                preceding fiscal year;
                    (C) the amounts deposited into or credited to the 
                Fund during the preceding fiscal year;
                    (D) the amount of earnings on investments of 
                amounts in the Fund during the preceding fiscal year;
                    (E) the amount paid from the Fund to pay for awards 
                made to whistleblowers pursuant to subsection (a) 
                during the preceding fiscal year;
                    (F) the balance of the Fund at the end of the 
                preceding fiscal year; and
                    (G) a complete set of audited financial statements, 
                including a balance sheet, income statement, and cash 
                flow analysis.
    (h) Rules of Construction.--
            (1) Original information.--Original information submitted 
        to the Commission by a whistleblower in accordance with the 
        requirements of this section shall not lose the status as 
        original information solely because the whistleblower submitted 
        the information before the effective date of any regulation 
        issued under this Act if the information was submitted after 
        the date of the enactment of this Act.
            (2) Awards.--A whistleblower--
                    (A) may receive an award pursuant to subsection (a) 
                regardless of whether the alleged covered violation 
                underlying the covered action occurred before the date 
                of the enactment of this Act; and
                    (B) may receive an award pursuant to subsection (a) 
                before the Commission promulgates any regulation 
                pursuant to this Act.

SEC. 4. RULEMAKING.

    The Commission may promulgate, under section 553 of title 5, United 
States Code, any regulations the Commission determines necessary to 
carry out the provisions of this Act.

SEC. 5. DEFINITIONS.

    In this Act:
            (1) Commission.--The term ``Commission'' means the Federal 
        Trade Commission.
            (2) Covered action.--The term ``covered action'' means any 
        administrative or judicial action or proceeding, including any 
        related administrative or judicial action, brought by the 
        Commission, or by the Attorney General on behalf of the 
        Commission, in relation to a covered violation and that results 
        in monetary sanctions exceeding $1,000,000.
            (3) Covered disclosure.--The term ``covered disclosure'' 
        means a formal or informal communication or transmission that 
        an individual reasonably believes relates to an alleged covered 
        violation, including such a communication or transmission of 
        such a violation that is part of the normal employment duties 
        of the individual.
            (4) Covered entity.--The term ``covered entity'' means an 
        entity or individual that is subject to the jurisdiction of the 
        Commission.
            (5) Covered violation.--The term ``covered violation'' 
        means--
                    (A) a violation of any law, rule, or regulation 
                enforced by the Commission; or
                    (B) a violation of any order of the Commission 
                after such order has become final and while such order 
                is in effect.
            (6) Fund.--The term ``Fund'' means the Federal Trade 
        Commission Consumer Protection Fund established pursuant to 
        section 3(g).
            (7) Monetary sanctions.--The term ``monetary sanctions'', 
        with respect to a covered action--
                    (A) means monies, including penalties, 
                disgorgement, or interest, ordered or agreed to be paid 
                as a result of such action; and
                    (B) does not include restitution (as determined by 
                the Commission) for losses of, or relief necessary to 
                redress injury to, consumers, other persons, 
                partnerships, and corporations.
            (8) Original information.--The term ``original 
        information'' means information that--
                    (A) is derived from the independent knowledge or 
                analysis of a whistleblower;
                    (B) is not known to the Commission from any other 
                source, unless the whistleblower is the original source 
                of the information; and
                    (C) is not exclusively derived from an allegation 
                made in a judicial or an administrative action, 
                governmental report, hearing, audit, or investigation, 
                or from the news media, unless the whistleblower is a 
                source of the information.
            (9) Qualified entity.--The term ``qualified entity'' 
        means--
                    (A) the Commission;
                    (B) an agency (as defined in section 551 of title 
                5, United States Code) or a law enforcement agency; or
                    (C) any Member of Congress or committee of 
                Congress.
            (10) Related administrative or judicial action.--The terms 
        ``related administrative action'' and ``related judicial 
        action'' include any action brought by any appropriate Federal 
        authority, a State attorney general in connection with any 
        criminal investigation, or any appropriate State regulatory 
        authority that is based upon the original information provided 
        by a whistleblower that leads to the successful enforcement of 
        the action by the Commission or the Attorney General on behalf 
        of the Commission.
            (11) Whistleblower.--The term ``whistleblower'' means--
                    (A) an individual (or group of individuals) who is 
                a current or former full-time, part-time, or temporary 
                employee, contractor, subcontractor (at any tier), 
                grantee, subgrantee, or agent of a covered entity or 
                employee of a contractor or subcontractor (at any tier) 
                of the covered entity and who engages in any of the 
                conduct described in paragraph (1), (2), or (3) of 
                section 2(a), including as part of the employment 
                duties of such individual or group; or
                    (B) any person that assists any such individual or 
                group with such conduct.

119th CONGRESS
  2d Session
                               H. R. 10794

To establish a grant program to make grants to States to improve access 
 to the special supplemental nutrition program for women, infants, and 
                               children.


_______________________________________________________________________


                    IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES

                            October 9, 2026

Mrs. Torres of California (for herself, Ms. Barragan, Ms. Bonamici, Ms. 
Clarke of New York, Mr. Costa, Ms. Crockett, Mr. Deluzio, Mrs. Dingell, 
    Ms. Garcia of Texas, Mrs. Grijalva, Mr. Ivey, Ms. Jayapal, Ms. 
  Kamlager-Dove, Ms. Kelly of Illinois, Mr. Kennedy of New York, Ms. 
Morrison, Ms. Norton, Ms. Pingree, Ms. Ross, Ms. Simon, Ms. Stansbury, 
  Ms. Tlaib, and Mr. Vargas) introduced the following bill; which was 
          referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce

_______________________________________________________________________

                                 A BILL


 
To establish a grant program to make grants to States to improve access 
 to the special supplemental nutrition program for women, infants, and 
                               children.

    Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the 
United States of America in Congress assembled,

SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE.

    This Act may be cited as the ``Improving Access to WIC Act''.

SEC. 2. GRANT PROGRAM TO IMPROVE ACCESS TO WIC.

    (a) Establishment.--Not later than 1 year after funds are first 
made available under subsection (g)(1), the Secretary shall carry out a 
grant program to make grants to each participating State agency for 
purposes of improving access to, and participation and retention in, 
the special supplemental nutrition program for women, infants, and 
children established under section 17 of the Child Nutrition Act of 
1966 (42 U.S.C. 1786) (in this section, referred to as ``WIC'').
    (b) Opt-In Participation.--The Secretary shall make a grant under 
subsection (a) to each State agency that opts in to the grant program 
by submitting an application at such time, in such manner, and 
containing such information as the Secretary may require.
    (c) Use of Funds.--A State agency that receives a grant under this 
section shall use the grant funds to carry out activities to improve 
access to, and participation and retention in, WIC. Such activities 
shall include at least one of the following:
            (1) Conducting outreach to potential participants in WIC, 
        including by--
                    (A) supporting direct referrals to WIC from 
                healthcare providers;
                    (B) establishing a statewide uniform process for 
                such direct referrals; and
                    (C) improving the notification of, or referral 
                systems for, such potential participants at Head Start 
                programs, preschools, elementary and secondary schools, 
                and such other programs or locations as the Secretary 
                determines appropriate.
            (2) Establishing, maintaining, or expanding statewide or 
        multi-statewide data-sharing guidelines to better allow 
        healthcare providers to--
                    (A) securely refer an individual to WIC; or
                    (B) with the consent of the individual, provide 
                local agencies with read-only access to the 
                individual's clinical data necessary for WIC 
                certification or participation.
            (3) Streamlining healthcare providers' ability to, subject 
        to applicable law and with the consent of the individual, send 
        such individual's height, weight, hemoglobin measurements, and 
        other WIC-related documentation, to local agencies for purposes 
        of WIC certification or participation.
            (4) Activities to improve the WIC enrollment experience, 
        including establishing or expanding an online application.
            (5) Only for the purposes of certifying eligible 
        individuals for WIC, identifying and contacting individuals who 
        receive medical assistance under title XIX of the Social 
        Security Act or are members of a household participating in the 
        supplemental nutrition assistance program established under the 
        Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 who are not currently 
        participating in WIC.
    (d) Limitation on Data Sharing.--Data collected pursuant to 
subsection (c) shall be--
            (1) used only for the purposes of--
                    (A) certifying eligible individuals for WIC;
                    (B) maintaining participation in WIC; or
                    (C) carrying out an activity specified in paragraph 
                (2)(B) or (3) of subsection (c); and
            (2) subject to the confidentiality provisions described in 
        section 246.26(d) of title 7, Code of Federal Regulations (or 
        successor regulations).
    (e) Distribution of Funds.--For each fiscal year in which funds are 
appropriated pursuant to paragraph (1) of subsection (g), a State 
agency participating the program under this section shall receive--
            (1) to the maximum extent practicable, an initial amount of 
        at least $200,000; and
            (2) an additional amount that bears the same proportion to 
        the amount appropriated for that fiscal year (less the amounts 
        reserved under subsection (g)(2) and distributed under 
        paragraph (1)) as the amount of participants in WIC in the 
        State served by the State agency bears to the amount of 
        participants in WIC in all States participating in the program, 
        as determined according to the most recent annual data 
        available.
    (f) Report.--Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment 
of this Act, and annually for each year subsequent to a year in which a 
grant is carried out under the program, the Secretary shall make 
publicly available on the website of the Department of Agriculture and 
submit to Congress a report--
            (1) on the outcomes of the program (including the impact of 
        the program on participation and retention in WIC); and
            (2) that includes best practices for establishing and 
        carrying out the activities under paragraphs (1) and (2) of 
        subsection (c).
    (g) Funding.--
            (1) Authorization of appropriations.--There is authorized 
        to be appropriated to carry out this section $50,000,000 for 
        each of fiscal year 2027 through 2031.
            (2) Reservation for administrative expenses.--The Secretary 
        may reserve not more than 5 percent of funds appropriated under 
        paragraph (1) for administrative expenses related to carrying 
        out this section.
    (h) Definitions.--In this section:
            (1) The term ``Head Start program''--
                    (A) means a program carried out under the Head 
                Start Act (42 U.S.C. 9831 et seq.); and
                    (B) includes Early Head Start programs.
            (2) The term ``local agency'' has the meaning given that 
        term in section 17 of the Child Nutrition Act of 1966 (42 
        U.S.C. 1786).
            (3) The term ``Secretary'' means the Secretary of 
        Agriculture.
            (4) The term ``State agency'' has the meaning given that 
        term in section 17 of the Child Nutrition Act of 1966 (42 
        U.S.C. 1786).
            (5) The term ``WIC'' means the special supplemental 
        nutrition program for women, infants, and children established 
        under section 17 of the Child Nutrition Act of 1966 (42 U.S.C. 
        1786).

                               H. R. 10795

To authorize the establishment of a United States-Sudan Agriculture and 
             Minerals partnership, and for other purposes.


_______________________________________________________________________


                    IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES

                            October 13, 2026

  Mr. Baird introduced the following bill; which was referred to the 
                      Committee on Foreign Affairs

_______________________________________________________________________

                                 A BILL


 
To authorize the establishment of a United States-Sudan Agriculture and 
             Minerals partnership, and for other purposes.

    Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the 
United States of America in Congress assembled,

SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE.

    This Act may be cited as the ``Sudan Investing in Minerals, 
Partnership, Agriculture, Commerce, and Trade Act'' or the ``Sudan 
IMPACT Act''.

SEC. 2. STATEMENT OF POLICY.

    To the extent that a legitimate, civilian-led governing authority 
in Sudan demonstrates that it has substantially reduced violence 
against its own civilians, it shall be the policy of the United States 
to partner with Sudan by providing agricultural exports and equipment, 
as well as safer, faster, and more efficient mining technologies, in 
exchange for access to Sudanese critical minerals.

SEC. 3. U.S.-SUDAN AGRICULTURE AND MINERALS PARTNERSHIP.

    (a) Establishment.--The Secretary of State shall seek to enter into 
a partnership between the United States and Sudan to expand economic 
engagement between the two countries. Such partnership shall be known 
as the ``United States-Sudan Agriculture and Minerals Partnership''.
    (b) Initial Improvements Threshold.--The Partnership established 
pursuant to subsection (a) may not be established until the Secretary 
of State determines that a legitimate, civilian-led governing authority 
in Sudan has taken sufficient steps to demonstrate measurable 
improvement with respect to--
            (1) civilian protection;
            (2) political stability; and
            (3) responsible governance of the resources with respect to 
        which activities under the partnership may be carried out.
    (c) Authorities Under Partnership.--Upon making an affirmative 
determination under subsection (b), the Secretary of State shall, 
pursuant to all appropriate authorities including authorities delegated 
to the Secretary under the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (22 U.S.C. 
2151 et seq.), establish a program under the Partnership through which, 
subject to the agreement of appropriate counterparts of a civilian-led 
Government of Sudan, the United States will make available to Sudan 
covered agricultural and mining equipment and assistance, in exchange 
for covered minerals mined or produced by Sudan.
    (d) Definitions.--In this Act:
            (1) The term ``covered agricultural and mining equipment 
        and assistance'' includes farm equipment, precision agriculture 
        and irrigation technology, agricultural processing equipment, 
        mining equipment, geological surveying technology and 
        assistance, mine safety technology, environmental remediation 
        technology, and supply-chain expertise.
            (2) The term ``covered minerals'' includes gold, uranium, 
        crude oil, chromium, iron, copper, manganese, zinc, silver, 
        nickel, and gum arabic.

                            October 13, 2026

  Mr. Bacon introduced the following bill; which was referred to the 
                      Committee on Armed Services

_______________________________________________________________________

                                 A BILL


 
  To direct the Secretary of the Air Force to carry out a program to 
provide for the safe, long-range aerial transport of individuals known 
    to be infected, or suspected of infection, by high-consequence 
                          infectious diseases.

    Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the 
United States of America in Congress assembled,

SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE.

    This Act may be cited as the ``Aerial Transport and High 
Consequence Infectious Diseases Act''.

SEC. 2. AERIAL TRANSPORT AND DEPARTMENT-WIDE CAPABILITY FOR HIGH-
              CONSEQUENCE INFECTIOUS DISEASES.

    (a) Requirement.--Beginning not later than October 1, 2027, the 
Secretary of the Air Force, in coordination with the Assistant 
Secretary of Defense for Health Affairs, the Secretaries of the other 
military departments, and the Director of the Defense Health Agency, 
shall carry out a Department program to provide for the safe, long-
range aerial transport of individuals known to be or suspected of 
infection by high-consequence infectious diseases.
    (b) Aerial Transport Component.--The Secretary of Defense shall 
ensure that the program under subsection (a) serves as the component of 
the Department of Defense that--
            (1) provides the Department with aerial transport of 
        patients with high-consequence infectious diseases; and
            (2) provides support to other departments and equivalent 
        program agencies of the Federal Government, State and local 
        governments, and civilian and academic partners, as determined 
        appropriate by the Secretary.
    (c) Program Requirements.--In carrying out the program under 
subsection (a), the Secretary of the Air Force shall--
            (1) develop and maintain a curriculum, and identify 
        qualified instructors to train and certify Department of 
        Defense medical personnel, on procedures associated with the 
        safe, long-range aerial transport of patients with high-
        consequence infectious diseases;
            (2) establish, and periodically update Department medical 
        care standards, infection prevention and control measures, and 
        operational safety protocols necessary to maximize patient 
        survival and minimize infection risk to aircrew, medical 
        personnel, and support personnel;
            (3) serve as the joint force advocate and executive agent 
        within the Department of Defense for aerial transport of 
        individuals with high-consequence infectious diseases;
            (4) establish standards, sustainment requirements, and 
        lifecycle management processes for personal protective 
        equipment, transport isolation systems, and associated medical 
        equipment used in transporting infected patients;
            (5) develop, in coordination with the Joint Staff, joint 
        doctrine, concepts of operation, and medical force requirements 
        necessary to support a Department of Defense-wide high-
        consequence infectious disease capability, including patient 
        movement, definitive care, and integration across the continuum 
        of care;
            (6) coordinate with the other Secretaries of the military 
        departments and the Director of the Defense Health Agency to 
        inform the organization, training, and equipping of 
        specialized, organized teams capable of conducting high-
        consequence infectious disease patient movement and care in 
        operational, austere, and strategic environments;
            (7) support the Department's role facilitating 
        interoperability and operational integration with other 
        departments and agencies of the Federal Government, State and 
        local governments, and civilian and academic partners to enable 
        coordinated response to tactical incidents, large-scale 
        contingencies, and research activities related to emerging and 
        future infectious disease threats; and
            (8) identify Department wide capability gaps and support 
        research, development, testing, and evaluation of medical 
        countermeasures, transport systems, protective equipment, and 
        operational procedures necessary to improve survivability, 
        safety, and mission effectiveness in high-consequence 
        infectious disease operations.
    (d) Enterprise Doctrine and Oversight.--The Secretary of Defense 
shall develop and maintain Department of Defense-wide doctrine and 
policy to guide the development, fielding, sustainment, and employment 
of high-consequence infectious disease response capabilities across the 
Department.

119th CONGRESS
  2d Session
                               H. R. 10802

  To direct heads of Federal agencies to support increased access to 
                    voting, and for other purposes.


_______________________________________________________________________


                    IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES

                            October 13, 2026

 Mr. Olszewski (for himself and Ms. McBride) introduced the following 
bill; which was referred to the Committee on House Administration, and 
   in addition to the Committees on Oversight and Government Reform, 
Science, Space, and Technology, Armed Services, and the Judiciary, for 
a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for 
consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the 
                          committee concerned

_______________________________________________________________________

                                 A BILL


 
  To direct heads of Federal agencies to support increased access to 
                    voting, and for other purposes.

    Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the 
United States of America in Congress assembled,

SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE.

    This Act may be cited as the ``Agency Support for Secure and 
Universal Registration Enhancement Act'' or the ``ASSURE Act''.

SEC. 2. CONSIDERATION OF AND STRATEGIC PLAN REGARDING VOTER 
              REGISTRATION AND PARTICIPATION.

    (a) Promotion of Voter Registration and Participation.--The head of 
each appropriate agency shall evaluate ways that the relevant agency 
can, as appropriate, promote voter registration and voter 
participation, including by considering--
            (1) ways to provide relevant information in the course of 
        activities or services that directly engage with the public 
        (including through agency materials, websites, online forms, 
        social media platforms, and other points of public access) 
        about how to register to vote, how to request a vote-by-mail 
        ballot, and how to cast a ballot in upcoming elections;
            (2) ways to facilitate seamless transition from agency 
        websites directly to State online voter registration systems or 
        appropriate Federal websites such as Vote.gov;
            (3) ways to provide access to voter registration services 
        and vote-by-mail ballot applications in the course of 
        activities or services that directly engage with the public, 
        including by--
                    (A) distributing voter registration and vote-by-
                mail ballot application forms and providing access to 
                applicable State online voter registration systems;
                    (B) assisting applicants in completing voter 
                registration and vote-by-mail ballot application forms 
                in a manner consistent with relevant State laws; and
                    (C) soliciting and facilitating covered nonprofit 
                organizations and State officials to provide voter 
                registration services on agency premises;
            (4) ways to promote and expand access to multilingual voter 
        registration and election information, and to promote equal 
        participation in the electoral process for eligible United 
        States citizens of all backgrounds; and
            (5) whether, consistent with applicable law, any identity 
        documents issued by the agency to members of the public can be 
        issued in a form that satisfies State voter identification 
        laws.
    (b) Strategic Plan.--Not later than 200 days after the date of the 
enactment of this Act, the head of each appropriate agency shall submit 
to the President and Congress a strategic plan outlining ways to 
promote voter registration and voter participation identified pursuant 
to the evaluation required in subsection (a).
    (c) Improvement of Federal Websites.--The Administrator of the 
Office of Electronic Government in the Office of Management and Budget 
shall coordinate efforts across agencies to improve or modernize 
Federal websites and digital services that provide Federal election and 
voting information, including ensuring that Federal websites are 
accessible to individuals with disabilities and individuals with 
limited English proficiency.
    (d) United States Digital Service Support.--As appropriate, the 
Administrator of the United States Digital Service may support agencies 
in implementing the strategic plans required in subsection (a).

SEC. 3. DESIGNATION UNDER THE NATIONAL VOTER REGISTRATION ACT.

    (a) Voter Registration Agency Designation.--
            (1) Designation agreement.--Each agency, if requested by a 
        State to be designated as a voter registration agency pursuant 
        to section 7(a)(3)(B)(ii) of the National Voter Registration 
        Act of 1993 (52 U.S.C. 20506(a)(3)(B)(ii)), shall, to the 
        greatest extent practicable, agree to such designation.
            (2) Designation declined.--If an agency declines to consent 
        to such designation, the head of the agency shall submit to the 
        President and Congress a written explanation for the decision 
        to decline.
    (b) Agreement to Designation Where Services Are Provided.--The head 
of each agency shall evaluate where and how the agency provides 
services that directly engage with the public and, to the greatest 
extent practicable, notify each State in which the agency provides such 
services that it would agree to designation as a voter registration 
agency pursuant to such section 7(a)(3)(B)(ii) (52 U.S.C. 
20506(a)(3)(B)(ii)).

SEC. 4. MODERNIZATION OF VOTE.GOV.

    (a) In General.--The Administrator of the General Services 
Administration shall modernize and improve the user experience of 
Vote.gov, in coordination with the Election Assistance Commission and 
appropriate Federal agencies and in consultation with affected 
stakeholders, including--
            (1) election administrators;
            (2) civil rights and disability rights advocates;
            (3) Tribal Nations; and
            (4) nonprofit groups that study best practices for using 
        technology to promote civic engagement.
    (b) Requirements.--In fulfilling the requirement in subsection (a), 
the Administrator shall--
            (1) ensure that Vote.gov complies, at minimum, with 
        sections 504 and 508 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (29 
        U.S.C. 794 and 794d); and
            (2) ensure that Vote.gov is translated into each language 
        spoken by a language minority group (as such term is used in 
        section 203 of the Voting Rights Act of 1965 (52 U.S.C. 10503)) 
        in the United States.
    (c) Strategic Plan.--Not later than 200 days after the date of the 
enactment of this Act, the Administrator shall submit to the President 
and Congress a strategic plan outlining the steps to modernize and 
improve the user experience of Vote.gov as required in subsection (a).

SEC. 5. VOTING OPPORTUNITIES FOR FEDERAL EMPLOYEES.

    Not later than 200 days after the date of the enactment of this 
Act, the Director of the Office of Personnel Management shall 
coordinate with the heads of executive agencies (as such term is 
defined in section 105 of title 5, United States Code) to provide 
recommendations to the President, through the Assistant to the 
President for Domestic Policy, on strategies to--
            (1) expand the Federal Government's policy of granting 
        employees time off to vote in Federal, State, local, Tribal, 
        and territorial elections (including to participate in early 
        voting); and
            (2) better support Federal employees who wish to volunteer 
        to serve as nonpartisan poll workers or nonpartisan observers, 
        particularly during early or extended voting periods.

SEC. 6. EQUAL ACCESS FOR VOTERS WITH DISABILITIES.

    Not later than 270 days after the date of the enactment of this 
Act, the National Institute of Standards and Technology shall publish--
            (1) the steps needed to ensure that Vote.gov is accessible 
        to people with disabilities; and
            (2) recommendations, developed in consultation with the 
        Department of Justice, the Election Assistance Commission, and 
        other agencies, as appropriate, regarding barriers to private 
        and independent voting for people with disabilities, including 
        access to voter registration, voting technology, voting by 
        mail, polling locations, and poll worker training.

SEC. 7. VOTING FOR ACTIVE DUTY MILITARY AND OVERSEAS CITIZENS.

    (a) Annual Requirement.--Not later than 200 days after the date of 
the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall--
            (1) establish procedures to affirmatively offer, on an 
        annual basis, each member of the Armed Forces on active duty 
        the opportunity to register to vote in Federal elections, 
        update voter registration information, or request an absentee 
        ballot; and
            (2) evaluate the feasibility of implementing an online 
        system to facilitate the services described in paragraph (1).
    (b) Ballot Tracking.--
            (1) In general.--The Secretary of Defense, in coordination 
        with the Department of State, the Military Postal Service 
        Agency, and the United States Postal Service, shall take all 
        practical steps to establish procedures to enable a 
        comprehensive end-to-end ballot tracking system for all 
        absentee ballots cast by absent uniformed services voters and 
        overseas voters (as such terms are defined in section 107 of 
        the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act (52 
        U.S.C. 20310)).
            (2) Strategic plan.--Not later than 200 days after the date 
        of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall 
        submit to the President and Congress a strategic plan for 
        establishing the ballot tracking system required in paragraph 
        (1).
    (c) Agency Coordination.--
            (1) In general.--The head of each agency with employees 
        stationed outside the United States shall designate an employee 
        to be responsible for coordinating with the Federal Voting 
        Assistance Program, including to promote voter registration and 
        voting services available to such employees.
            (2) Office of management and budget assistance.--The 
        Director of the Office of Management and Budget may issue 
        guidance to assist agencies in making the designations required 
        in paragraph (1).

SEC. 8. VOTER REGISTRATION FOR ELIGIBLE INDIVIDUALS IN FEDERAL CUSTODY.

    (a) Federal Bureau of Prisons.--
            (1) In general.--The Attorney General shall establish 
        procedures to provide educational materials related to voter 
        registration and voting and, to the extent practicable, to 
        facilitate voter registration, for all eligible individuals in 
        the custody of the Federal Bureau of Prisons.
            (2) Educational materials.--The educational materials 
        required in paragraph (1) shall--
                    (A) be incorporated into the reentry planning 
                procedures required under section 4042(a)(7) of title 
                18, United States Code; and
                    (B) notify each individual leaving Federal custody 
                of--
                            (i) any restriction on the ability of such 
                        individual to vote under the laws of the State 
                        where the individual resides; and
                            (ii) if any such restrictions exist, the 
                        point at which such restriction will be lifted 
                        under applicable State law.
    (b) Contracts and Agreements.--The Attorney General shall establish 
procedures--
            (1) to ensure the United States Marshals Service includes 
        language in intergovernmental agreements and jail contracts to 
        require the jails to provide educational materials related to 
        voter registration and voting, and to facilitate voting by 
        mail, to the extent practicable and appropriate; and
            (2) for coordinating with the Probation and Pretrial 
        Services Office of the Administrative Office of the United 
        States Courts to provide educational materials related to voter 
        registration and voting to all eligible individuals under the 
        supervision of the Probation and Pretrial Services Office, and 
        to facilitate voter registration and voting by such 
        individuals.
    (c) Identification.--The Attorney General shall take appropriate 
steps to support formerly incarcerated individuals in obtaining 
identification that satisfies State voter identification laws, 
including as required by section 4042(a)(6)(B) of title 18, United 
States Code.

SEC. 9. NATIVE AMERICAN VOTING RIGHTS STEERING GROUP.

    (a) Establishment.--There is established an Interagency Steering 
Group on Native American Voting Rights (in this section referred to as 
the ``Steering Group''), coordinated by the Domestic Policy Council, 
which shall engage in meaningful and robust consultation with Tribal 
Nations and Native leaders regarding concerns and potential areas of 
focus for the report required in subsection (d).
    (b) Membership.--
            (1) In general.--The Steering Group shall be chaired by the 
        Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy and shall 
        include the Attorney General, the Secretary of the Interior, 
        the Secretary of Agriculture, the Secretary of Labor, the 
        Secretary of Health and Human Services, and the Secretary of 
        Veterans Affairs.
            (2) Optional participation.--The Chair may invite heads or 
        senior representatives of other agencies to participate in the 
        Steering Group.
    (c) Consultation With Other Agencies.--The Steering Group shall 
consult with agencies not represented on the Steering Group to 
facilitate the sharing of information and best practices, as 
appropriate.
    (d) Public Report.--Not later than 1 year after the date of the 
enactment of this Act, the Steering Group shall make publically 
available a report describing best practices for protecting voting 
rights of Native Americans and outlining recommendations for providing 
such protection, including recommendations for--
            (1) increasing voter outreach, education, registration, and 
        turnout in Native American communities;
            (2) increasing voting access for Native American 
        communities (including increasing accessibility for voters with 
        disabilities);
            (3) mitigating internet accessibility issues that may 
        hinder voter registration and ballot access in Native American 
        communities;
            (4) increasing language access and assistance for Native 
        American voters, including evaluating existing best practices;
            (5) mitigating barriers to voting for Native Americans by 
        analyzing and providing guidance on how to facilitate the use 
        of Tribal government identification cards as valid voter 
        identification in Federal, State, local, Tribal, and 
        territorial elections;
            (6) facilitating collaboration among local election 
        officials, Native American communities, and Tribal election 
        offices; and
            (7) addressing other areas identified through the 
        consultation required in subsection (a).
    (e) Administrative Support.--The Department of the Interior shall 
provide administrative support for the Steering Group.
    (f) Sunset.--The Steering Group established in this section shall 
terminate on the day after the report is made publically available 
under subsection (d).

SEC. 10. NONGOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS AT NATURALIZATION CEREMONIES.

    The Director of the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services shall 
permit any covered nonprofit organization to provide voter registration 
applications and general information regarding voting to new United 
States citizens at an administrative naturalization ceremony.

SEC. 11. DEFINITIONS.

    In this Act:
            (1) Agency.--The term ``agency'' has the meaning given such 
        term in section 3502 of title 44, United States Code, except 
        that such term does not include any independent regulatory 
        agency (as such term is defined in such section).
            (2) Covered nonprofit organization.--The term ``covered 
        nonprofit organization'' means an organization that--
                    (A) is described in section 501(c) of the Internal 
                Revenue Code of 1986 and exempt from tax under section 
                501(a) of such Code; and
                    (B) commits to not participate in any political 
                activity, partisan or otherwise, at an administrative 
                naturalization ceremony or while providing voter 
                registration services on an agency premises.

119th CONGRESS
  2d Session
                               H. R. 10807

    To prohibit the use of automated mass surveillance systems and 
             associated components, and for other purposes.


_______________________________________________________________________


                    IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES

                            October 13, 2026

 Ms. Tlaib (for herself, Ms. Garcia of Texas, Ms. Lee of Pennsylvania, 
    Ms. Omar, Mrs. Ramirez, Ms. Velazquez, and Mrs. Watson Coleman) 
 introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on 
 Oversight and Government Reform, and in addition to the Committee on 
   the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the 
  Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall 
           within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned

_______________________________________________________________________

                                 A BILL


 
    To prohibit the use of automated mass surveillance systems and 
             associated components, and for other purposes.

    Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the 
United States of America in Congress assembled,

SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE.

    This Act may be cited as the ``Get the Flock Out of Our Communities 
Act''.

SEC. 2. PROHIBITION ON USE OF AUTOMATED MASS SURVEILLANCE SYSTEMS.

    (a) Prohibition on Use of Federal Funds.--Notwithstanding any other 
provision of law, no Federal funds made available before, on, or after 
the date of the enactment of this Act for any fiscal year or otherwise 
made available to any agency, State, or unit of local government may be 
obligated, expended, reprogrammed, or transferred to purchase, deploy, 
install, maintain, access, lease, or operate any automated mass 
surveillance system, including any of the following:
            (1) Automatic license plate reader or associated component.
            (2) Biometric surveillance system.
            (3) Facial recognition technology.
    (b) Prohibition on Use of Automated Mass Surveillance Systems.--An 
agency, or employee or officer of an agency acting in an official 
capacity may not acquire, possess, access, solicit, or use in the 
United States--
            (1) any automated mass surveillance system; or
            (2) information derived from an automated mass surveillance 
        system.
    (c) Removal.--Each agency, State, or unit of local government that 
purchases, deploys, installs, maintains, leases or operates or is in 
the process of purchasing, deploying, installing, maintaining, leasing, 
or operating any automated mass surveillance system using Federal funds 
shall remove or order a lessee to remove any such automated mass 
surveillance system not later than 30 days after the date of the 
enactment of this Act.
    (d) Disposal of Data.--An agency, State, or unit of local 
government or employee or officer of an agency, State, or unit of local 
government acting in an official capacity that possesses automated mass 
surveillance data prohibited under subsections (a) or (b) shall 
permanently delete such data not later than 7 days after the date of 
the enactment of this Act.
    (e) Inadmissibility.--Any data obtained in violation of this 
section may not be admitted into evidence in any court or 
administrative proceeding.
    (f) Eligibility for Certain Federal Grants.--
            (1) Certification required for certain grants.--An 
        application by a State or a unit of local government for 
        funding under a covered program shall include a certification 
        that such State, unit of local government, and any law 
        enforcement agency to which the State or unit of local 
        government will distribute funds, does not maintain, access, 
        lease, or operate any automated mass surveillance system or 
        information derived from an automated mass surveillance system.
            (2) Eligibility for certain grants.--A State or unit of 
        local government shall be ineligible for funding under a 
        covered program without providing the certification described 
        under subsection (b).
    (g) Definitions.--In this section:
            (1) Agency.--The term ``agency'' has the meaning given that 
        term in section 551 of title 5, United States Code.
            (2) Associated component.--The term ``associated 
        component'', with respect to an automated mass surveillance 
        system, includes any product, service, hardware, software, 
        algorithm, database, communications network, cloud-based 
        service, or data analysis platform of, or used in connection 
        with, such system to collect, store, process, analyze, compare, 
        query, match, transmit, share, or retrieve data collected or 
        generated by such system, including biometric data.
            (3) Automated mass surveillance system.--The term 
        ``automated mass surveillance system'' means any automated 
        system or technology that acquires, processes, collects, 
        analyzes, generates, retains, uses, or stores information or 
        data on an indefinite or large number of people.
            (4) Automatic license plate reader.--The term ``automatic 
        license plate reader'' means any camera or camera system 
        product or service that automatically captures license plate 
        data of vehicles, and any associated information.
            (5) Biometric surveillance system.--The term ``biometric 
        surveillance system'' means any computer software that performs 
        facial recognition or other remote biometric recognition in 
        real time or on a recording or photograph that allows or 
        confirms the unique identification or verification of an 
        individual and is generated from the measurement or processing 
        of unique biological, physical, or physiological 
        characteristics, including any of the following:
                    (A) Fingerprint.
                    (B) Voice print.
                    (C) Iris or retina imagery scan.
                    (D) Facial or hand mapping, geometry, or template.
                    (E) Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA).
                    (F) Gait.
            (6) Byrne grant program.--The term ``Byrne grant program'' 
        means any grant program under subpart 1 of part E of title I of 
        the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 (34 
        U.S.C. 10151 et seq.), without regard to whether the funds are 
        characterized as being made available under the Edward Byrne 
        Memorial State and Local Law Enforcement Assistance Programs, 
        the Local Government Law Enforcement Block Grants Program, the 
        Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant Program, or 
        otherwise.
            (7) Cops grant program.--The term ``COPS grant program'' 
        means the grant program authorized under section 1701 of title 
        I of the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 (34 
        U.S.C. 10381).
            (8) Covered program.--The term ``covered program'' means 
        any program or activity funded in whole or in part with funds 
        made available under--
                    (A) a Byrne grant program; and
                    (B) the COPS grant program.
            (9) Facial recognition technology.--The term ``facial 
        recognition technology'' means technology that facilitates or 
        otherwise enables an automated or semi-automated process that 
        assists in identifying an individual based on the physical 
        characteristics of the face of the individual, or that logs 
        characteristics of the face, head, or body of an individual to 
        infer emotion, associations, activities, or the location of an 
        individual.
            (10) State.--The term ``State'' means each of the several 
        States, the District of Columbia, and each commonwealth, 
        territory, or possession of the United States.

119th CONGRESS
  2d Session
                               H. R. 10816

   To amend title 10, United States Code, to prohibit the naming of 
  Department of Defense assets for sitting Presidents, and for other 
                               purposes.


_______________________________________________________________________


                    IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES

                            October 15, 2026

  Mrs. Dingell (for herself, Mr. Mfume, and Mr. Bell) introduced the 
 following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Armed Services

_______________________________________________________________________

                                 A BILL


 
   To amend title 10, United States Code, to prohibit the naming of 
  Department of Defense assets for sitting Presidents, and for other 
                               purposes.

    Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the 
United States of America in Congress assembled,

SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE.

    This Act may be cited as ``Department of Defense Renaming Integrity 
and Ethics Act of 2026'' or the ``DORIE Act of 2026''.

SEC. 2. PROHIBITION ON NAMING OF DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE ASSETS FOR 
              SITTING PRESIDENTS.

    (a) In General.--Chapter 2 of title 10, United States Code, is 
amended by adding at the end the following new section:
``Sec. 120a. Prohibition on naming of Department of Defense assets for 
              sitting Presidents
    ``Notwithstanding any other provision of law--
            ``(1) no facility, aircraft, vessel, or other asset of the 
        Department of Defense may be named, renamed, designated, or 
        redesignated in the name of a sitting President; and
            ``(2) none of the amounts authorized to be appropriated or 
        otherwise made available for the Department of Defense for any 
        fiscal year may be used to name, rename, designate, or 
        redesignate any facility, aircraft, vessel, or other asset of 
        the Department of Defense in the name of a sitting 
        President.''.
    (b) Applicability.--Any facility, aircraft, vessel, or other asset 
of the Department of Defense that, as of the date of the enactment of 
this Act, is named for the individual who is the President on such date 
shall be restored to the name of such facility, aircraft, vessel, or 
other asset immediately before the facility, aircraft, vessel, or other 
asset was named, renamed, designated, or redesignated in the name of a 
sitting President.

119th CONGRESS
